questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Several aspects were crucial when I chose to study in Sydney. I wanted to go to an English speaking country, and I also wanted to explore a new place and have lots of amazing travelling/nature experiences, which Australia has. I also wished to go to a good university which would be relevant on my resumé, but this was not my first priority.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I had a really good experience. Academically, it has not been my most interesting semester. My sense is that Australia is not as good at receiving international students and creating social places for them to meet as many other places, so I had to take a more active approach in making friends, and I knew a lot of people from back home, which was also nice in the beginning.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was quite hard at times - there are a lot of questions where you cannot find the answer anywhere. But I figured out that KU helped me a lot when it came to the important stuff, so everything worked out in the end. But it is a good idea to talk to someone who has been abroad already to help the process.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I received help on getting the right courses (I had not finalized this from home, which I was upset about). My student coordinator in Sydney helped me A LOT, and KU helped me as well.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: They were very helpful with my courses

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: There were some university colleges (but my sense is that these are mostly for Australian students). Scape is also an option, but is VERY expensive. I choose the cheapest on-campus option, Queen Mary, which was fine, not the best - but it is close to Newtown, which is a great part of Sydney, and in walking-distance to the university. And there are almost only other international students, why it was a fun place to live.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: Cooking facilities only at Queen Mary. I think some of the other campus housing options has meal plans available.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: I think it is a great way to meet other international students. But many international students in Sydney find their own housing off-campus, and it is often the same price with better facilities. But of course it depends.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I liked living on campus

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: We were guided through the process

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It was easy to find courses at University of Sydney, the hardest part was just knowing what would be accepted by KU

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I had a student coordinator at the University

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got the classes I wanted

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: It was easiest for me to get the courses when I arrived in Sydney (I had problems before, but I set up an in-person meeting when I arrived in Sydney). You can change your subjects up to two weeks after arriving in Sydney.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The academic level was lower than at KU

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I took three 3rd-year economic courses: Public Finance, Strategic Behaviour (Mikro III), and Development Economics, and they were not on a higher level than at KU. It was very straightforward. I also had a first-year course, History and Philosophy of Science.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: There was participation requirements in Philosophy of science, and mid-term exams that counted towards the final grade, which was different. But I liked this, as we had less pressure on the final exam.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Public Finance, Development Economics, Strategic Behaviour (Mikro III) and What's This Thing Called Science? (Videnskabsteori).

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I liked that I got 4 mandatory courses - but I cannot recommend development economics, it was not very interesting and I would have preferred taking a more interesting elective course instead.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: There is a mandatory health ensurance, which was a little expensive. The visa was also a little expensive. There were a bunch of fees of my campus housing.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Basically the same level as in Denmark, some things are more expensive and some things are cheaper

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I did not really find any suitable clubs for me. I tried to join the Tennis Club, but it seemed to be closed down

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I did not find any suitable for me, but there are definitely some

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I heard that the Skiing club should be fun to be a part of (they don't go skiing, but it is a fun society)

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Uluru was the biggest experience. Furthermore, you should go to Blue Mountains and maybe Byron Bay

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Easy. I mostly hung out with other Danish people and Scandinavian people.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I did not really socialize with local students

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Nothing particular

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Outgoing, down-to-earth people

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: That everything will be fine! I had a million questions about how everything practical would work out, but it was all fine in the end.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Nothing particular

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Travelling around and the people I met

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Meeting new people during the first couple of weeks! But after this, everything was fine.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: No comments

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
